answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching vendors or adding a second source now carries unacceptable onboarding/delivery risk. Deferring is also unattractive because the contract does not auto-renew, unlike the prior non-critical deferral case. Renegotiating with the incumbent (supported by memory_c4's benchmarking success and memory_c6's multi-year volume pricing gains) offers a path to meet the 18% spend-cut mandate while preserving supply continuity and integration stability. I verify c4 and c6 because they are the load-bearing evidence for expecting real margin recovery via negotiation rather than assuming success from consolidated summaries alone.
